rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permitted guardian-orphan mixing should resemble two brothers sharing social rights equally, with what is taken from the orphan's property balanced by what is given.
rows.anchor: فالذي تجوزه الآية في مخالطة الولي لليتيم أن يكون كالمخالطة بين الأخوين المتساويين في الحقوق الاجتماعية بين الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse parallels the command not to consume orphan property with one's own; this parallel, its ending, and God's knowledge of reformers and corrupters signal a concession and easing.
rows.anchor: فالآية تحاذي قوله تعالى وآتوا اليتامى أموالهم ولا تتبدلوا الخبيث بالطيب ولا تأكلوا أموالهم إلى أموالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If mixing is necessary, it should be genuinely for reform like equal brotherly dealings; guardians need not fear mere mixing, since God distinguishes reform from corruption.
rows.anchor: ولا ينبغي عند ذلك الخوف والخشية، فإن ذلك لو كان بغرض الإصلاح حقيقة لا صورة كان من الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction with min after يعلم is explained by embedding the sense of يميز, to distinguish one from the other.
rows.anchor: تعدية يعلم بمن كأنها لمكان تضمينه معنى يميز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: العنت means burden, hardship, or difficulty.
rows.anchor: يميز، والعنت هو الكلفة والمشقة

rows.speaker: علي بن يقطين
rows.claim: Ali ibn Yaqtin recounts the Mahdi questioning Abu al-Hasan about wine's Qur'anic prohibition; the Imam identifies Qur'anic sin with wine and cites 2:219, and the Mahdi acknowledges the Ahl al-Bayt's learning.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن يقطين قال سأل المهدي أبا الحسن عليه السلام عن الخمر هل هي محرمة

rows.speaker: أحدهما عليهما السلام
rows.claim: One of the two Imams describes sin as a house with a door and lock, and wine as its key.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أحدهما عليهما السلام قال إن الله جعل للمعصية بيتا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet calls wine the head of every sin.
rows.anchor: إن الخمر رأس كل إثم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: When Quraysh ask which sin is greatest, Imam al-Baqir answers that drinking wine is the greatest.
rows.anchor: عن إسماعيل قال أقبل أبو جعفر عليه السلام في المسجد الحرام فنظر إليه قوم من قريش

rows.speaker: أحدهما عليهما السلام
rows.claim: One of the two Imams says no act disobeys God more severely than drinking intoxicants, which can lead an unaware drinker to abandon prayer and commit incest.
rows.anchor: عن أبي البلاد عن أحدهما عليهما السلام قال ما عصي الله بشيء أشد من شرب المسكر

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Answering why wine is forbidden despite its pleasure, Imam al-Sadiq says it is the mother of abominations and head of evil, removing reason and leading to every sin.
rows.anchor: سأل زنديق أبا عبد الله عليه السلام لم حرم الله الخمر ولا لذة أفضل منها؟ قال حرمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports explain one another, and experience and reflection confirm them.
rows.anchor: أقول والروايات تفسر بعضها بعضا، والتجارب والاعتبار يساعدانها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet curses ten participants in the wine trade, from its grower and keeper through its drinker, seller, buyer, and consumer of its price.
rows.anchor: عن جابر عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال لعن رسول الله في الخمر عشرة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet curses anyone who sits at a table where wine is being drunk.
rows.anchor: وفي الكافي والمحاسن عن الصادق عليه السلام قال قال رسول الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says God will not look on Judgment Day at four people: a disobedient child, a benefactor who reminds recipients of the gift, a denier of predestination, and a habitual wine drinker.
rows.anchor: وفي الخصال بإسناده عن أبي أمامة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says a wine drinker will receive an equal measure of boiling punishment in the afterlife, whether forgiven or punished, and describes the drinker's appearance on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وفي الأمالي لابن الشيخ بإسناده عن الصادق عليه السلام عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Imam al-Baqir says wine drinkers will be given a hellish drink made from the discharge of prostitutes, which he describes as pus and thick mixed blood.
rows.anchor: في تفسير القمي عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال حق على الله أن يسقي من يشرب الخمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threats in the wine reports may be supported by the Qur'anic description of the sinner's food and boiling punishment.
rows.anchor: خذوه فاعتلوه إلى سواء الجحيم

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن عليه السلام
rows.claim: Imam al-Rida identifies al-maysir as gambling.
rows.anchor: وفي الكافي عن الوشا عن أبي الحسن عليه السلام قال سمعته يقول الميسر هو القمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Numerous reports support identifying al-maysir with gambling, a meaning the author regards as beyond doubt.
rows.anchor: أقول والروايات في هذا المعنى كثيرة لا غبار عليها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that companions ordered to spend in God's cause asked how much to give; the verse answered that they should give the surplus, after one man had given away even what he needed to eat.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس إن نفرا من الصحابة حين أمروا بالنفقة في سبيل الله أتوا النبي

rows.speaker: يحيى
rows.claim: Yahya reports that Muadh ibn Jabal and Tha'laba, supporting dependents and servants, asked the Prophet how much of their property to spend, prompting the verse.
rows.anchor: عن يحيى أنه بلغه أن معاذ بن جبل وثعلبة أتيا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Imam al-Sadiq glosses al-afw as the middle amount.
rows.anchor: عن الصادق عليه السلام العفو الوسط

rows.speaker: الباقر والصادق عليهما السلام
rows.claim: Imams al-Baqir and al-Sadiq explain al-afw as enough for subsistence.
rows.anchor: عن الباقر والصادق عليهما السلام الكفاف

rows.speaker: أبو بصير
rows.claim: A report from Abu Basir glosses al-afw as moderation or a reasonable amount.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أبي بصير القصد

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Imam al-Sadiq relates the spending verse to the description of those who spend neither extravagantly nor stingily, saying this is the moderate course.
rows.anchor: وفيه أيضا عن الصادق عليه السلام في الآية الذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا وكان بين ذلك قواما

rows.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Imam al-Baqir defines al-afw as what remains beyond a year's provision.
rows.anchor: في المجمع عن الباقر عليه السلام العفو ما فضل عن قوت السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported glosses are compatible; the annual-provision account specifies an instance of the meaning.
rows.anchor: أقول والروايات متوافقة، والأخيرة من قبيل بيان المصداق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports on charity's virtues, proper manner, recipients, and amount are too numerous to count and will be cited where relevant later.
rows.anchor: والروايات في فضل الصدقة وكيفيتها وموردها وكميتها فوق حد الإحصاء

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: After the warning against wrongful consumption of orphans' wealth, guardians expelled the orphans they housed and asked the Prophet what to do; the present verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن الصادق عليه السلام قال إنه لما نزلت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says guardians separated orphans' food and drink, saving leftovers until they were eaten or spoiled and discarded; after the hardship was reported, this verse permitted them to share food and drink.
rows.anchor: وفي الدر المنثور عن ابن عباس قال لما أنزل الله

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، عطاء، قتادة
rows.claim: The same account of the hardship caused by separating orphans' provisions and the ensuing permission to mix them is also transmitted from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ata, and Qatada.
rows.anchor: وروي هذا المعنى عن سعيد بن جبير وعطاء وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage presents divine unity and therefore relates to what precedes; it may have been revealed together with the preceding verses.
rows.anchor: الآيات مشتملة على معنى التوحيد ولذلك كانت غير خالية عن الارتباط بما قبلها من الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muhajjah is setting proof against proof to establish a claim or refute its opposite; the root sense of hujja is intention, later conventionally a proof for a claim.
rows.anchor: المحاجة إلقاء الحجة قبال الحجة لإثبات المدعي أو لإبطال ما يقابله، وأصل الحجة هو القصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase fi rabbihi is governed by hajjah, and its pronoun refers to Abraham, as the later words about Abraham's Lord show.
rows.anchor: وقوله في ربه متعلق بحاج، والضمير لإبراهيم كما يشعر به قوله تعالى فيما بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disputant is Nimrod, a Babylonian king contemporary with Abraham, as history and reports state.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي حاج إبراهيم عليه السلام في ربه هو الملك الذي كان يعاصره وهو نمرود من ملوك بابل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings are innately subject to powers superior to them and effective in their lives, a pattern apparent across past nations and present communities.
rows.anchor: إن الإنسان لا يزال خاضعا بحسب الفطرة للقوى المستعلية عليه، المؤثرة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By innate disposition people affirm a maker who affects the world's creation and governance, whether they are monotheists, polytheists, or deniers; fitra is never falsified, though people may neglect it.
rows.anchor: وهو بفطرته يثبت للعالم صانعا مؤثرا فيه بحسب التكوين والتدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Early people analogized from themselves, assigned different events to distinct causes, and consequently posited gods of species and planets, using idols as intermediaries; differing cultures formed differing images and cults.
rows.anchor: لما كان يقيس الأشياء إلى نفسه، وكان يرى من نفسه أن أفعاله المختلفة تستند إلى قواه وأعضائه المختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People gradually clung to sensory idols and forgot the beings represented, even the supreme God; powerful rulers exploited popular belief to claim divinity, while their visible power made them seem superior to other gods.
rows.anchor: وربما انجر الأمر تدريجا إلى التشبث بالأصنام ونسيان أربابها حتى رب الأرباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's claim to be the highest lord shows that he asserted supremacy while still recognizing other gods.
rows.anchor: كما يحكيه الله تعالى من قول فرعون لقومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod too claimed divinity and superiority over other gods; the author infers this from his claim to give life and death, while Pharaoh's reference to his gods shows the rulers could retain a pantheon.
rows.anchor: وكذلك كان يدعي نمرود على ما يستفاد من قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod's actual dispute was over exclusive lordship: Abraham said only God was his Lord, while Nimrod claimed to be lord of Abraham and others and worthy of their worship.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يستنتج أن المحاجة التي وقعت بينه وبين إبراهيم عليه السلام هي، أن إبراهيم عليه السلام كان يدعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod's reply means that he himself was the Lord Abraham described; he said أنا أحيي وأميت without a coordinating 'and' because he sought exclusive superiority, not partnership in God's lordship.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل وأنا أحيي وأميت، لأن لازم العطف أن يشارك الله في ربوبيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod also did not mention the other gods, since his aim was to claim that he alone outranked them.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل أيضا والآلهة تحيي وتميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod answers by deception, not a valid counterproof: Abraham meant the observable literal origin and removal of life in conscious, willing creatures.
rows.anchor: ولم يعارض إبراهيم عليه السلام بالحق، بل بالتمويه والمغالطة وتلبيس الأمر على من حضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nature of life is unknown, but only a possessor of life can originate it; inert nature and other living beings cannot explain it, since no thing creates or annihilates itself.
rows.anchor: فإن هذه الحياة المجهولة لكنه لا يستطيع أن يوجدها إلا من هو واجد لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod equivocated by taking life and death metaphorically or broadly: he ordered two prisoners brought, killed one, released the other, and presented this as giving death and life.
rows.anchor: وعند ذلك أمر بإحضار رجلين من السجن فأمر بقتل أحدهما وإطلاق الآخر فقتل هذا واطلق ذاك فقال أنا أحيي وأميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham could not expose the equivocation because he saw Nimrod's sham and the audience's blind acceptance; he therefore changed to a proof the obstinate opponent could not answer.
rows.anchor: فوجد أنه لو بين وجه المغالطة لم يصدقه أحد، فعدل إلى حجة أخرى لا يدع المكابر أن يعارضه بشيء

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْتِى بِٱلشَّمْسِ مِنَ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if Nimrod's people treated the sun as a god, its rising and setting ultimately depend on the Lord of lords; a voluntary agent can choose otherwise, so Nimrod must bring it from the west.
rows.anchor: وذلك ان الشمس وإن كانت من جملة الآلهة عندهم أو عند بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod could not call the sun's regular eastern rising accidental, attribute it to the sun independently of God, or claim to cause it himself; he was silenced and confounded.
rows.anchor: ما كان يسعه أن يقول إن هذا الأمر المستمر الجاري على وتيرة واحدة وهو طلوعها من المشرق دائما أمر اتفاقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase an atahu Allah al-mulk has an omitted lām of causation, and uses a favor as the apparent cause of Nimrod's aggression to express complaint and accusation.
rows.anchor: الجملة أعني قوله أن آتاه الله الملك بتقدير لام التعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod's tyranny should have been attributed to the opposite of divine beneficence, but only God's kindness and gift of kingship is named, exposing his ingratitude.
rows.anchor: فإن عدوان نمرود وطغيانه في هذه المحاجة كان ينبغي أن يعلل بضد إنعام الله عليه

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited verse says the sons repaid Abu al-Ghaylan's advanced age and good deed as Sanmar was repaid, illustrating the ironic reversal of kindness.
rows.anchor: جزى بنوه أبا الغيلان عن كبر وحسن فعل كما يجزى سنمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same reversal appears in Pharaoh's family taking Moses as a child so that he would become their enemy and grief.
rows.anchor: فهو بوجه كقوله تعالى فالتقطه آل فرعون ليكون لهم عدوا وحزنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another purpose of mentioning the gift is to expose the claim's weakness: Nimrod's authority came from God, and as a person he was otherwise unremarkable, hence the text leaves him unnamed.
rows.anchor: إنما كان نمرود الملك ذا السلطة والسطوة بنعمة من ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kingship is a divinely bestowed capacity and innate human aspiration: used rightly it brings felicity, but exceeding its bounds turns it into ruin.
rows.anchor: فإن الملك وهو نوع سلطنة منبسطة على الأمة كسائر أنواع السلطنة والقدرة نعمة من الله وفضل يؤتيه من يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing a thing to God is appropriate from its good aspect, not its evil or harmful aspect.
rows.anchor: لكل شيء نسبة إليه تعالى على ما يليق بساحة قدسه تعالى وتقدس من جهة الحسن الذي فيه دون جهة القبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects exegetes who take the pronoun in 'that God gave him kingship' to refer to Abraham and the kingship to be Abraham's.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر سقوط ما ذكره بعض المفسرين ان الضمير في قوله أن آتاه الله الملك،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham did not argue from the world's dependence on its creator as he had when first recognizing God, because the people could not understand that proof adequately; their misunderstanding of his simpler life-and-death argument shows this.
rows.anchor: فإن القوم على اعترافهم بذلك بفطرتهم إجمالا كانوا أنزل سطحا من أن يعقلوه على ما ينبغي أن يعقل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod means, 'I am your Lord,' the one who possesses the life-and-death power Abraham attributed to his Lord.
rows.anchor: أي فأنا ربك الذي وصفته بأنه يحيي ويميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the first proof was twisted, Abraham builds the solar challenge on Nimrod's own claim, signaled by fa; he says Allah rather than 'my Lord' to block another misapplication of the wording.
rows.anchor: إلا أنه بنى هذه الحجة الثانية على دعوى الخصم في الحجة الأولى كما يدل عليه التفريع بالفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause explains Nimrod's defeat: God did not guide him, so he was confounded; it does not say lack of guidance caused his disbelief, and the context concerns the debate.
rows.anchor: وبعبارة أخرى معناه أن الله لم يهده فبهت لذلك ولو هداه لغلب على إبراهيم في الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them wrongdoers suggests that their wrongdoing is the cause of God's withholding guidance, as in other occurrences of this Qur'anic wording.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن في الوصف إشعارا بالعلية أعني أن السبب لعدم هداية الله الظالمين هو ظلمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the command to leave scoffers engrossed in play until their promised day as part of the account of the disbelievers' condition.
rows.anchor: فذرهم يخوضوا ويلعبوا حتى يلاقوا يومهم الذي يوعدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unveiling of a person's cover and sharpening of sight is cited in the discussion of how perception changes.
rows.anchor: لقد كنت في غفلة من هذا فكشفنا عنك غطاءك فبصرك اليوم حديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic command to turn away from one who rejects remembrance and seeks only worldly life identifies that as the limit of such people's knowledge.
rows.anchor: فأعرض عمن تولى عن ذكرنا ولم يرد إلا الحياة الدنيا ذلك مبلغهم من العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite worldly enjoyments, disbelievers' lives are never wholly clear of distress; they are clouded by greater grief and worry.
rows.anchor: على أنهم لا يصفو لهم عيش إلا وهو منغص بما يربو عليه من الغم والهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Perception and thought among God's people, especially those shaped by the Qur'an, differ from those of others despite their common humanity; believers who lack complete divine teaching and discipline occupy intermediate degrees.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن الإدراك والفكر الموجود في أهل الله وخاصة القرآن غيرهما في غيرهم مع كونهم جميعا من نوع واحد هو الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scripture also calls bodily misery punishment, but it is punishment at the bodily level rather than the spiritual one; Job's complaint is an example.
rows.anchor: لكن نهايته أنه عذاب في مرحلة الجسم دون الروح قال تعالى حكاية عن أيوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suffering imposed by Pharaoh's people, including killing sons and sparing women, is called punishment and a trial from God, while the punishment itself is not an act directly perpetrated by God.
rows.anchor: فسمى ما يصنعون بهم بلاء وامتحانا من الله وعذابا في نفسه لا منه سبحانه

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَيْهِ شَىْءٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's complete knowledge clarifies the preceding description of Him as mighty and avenging: otherwise He might fail to know some denials of His favor and not punish them.
rows.anchor: قد علل تعالى عذاب الذين كفروا بآياته بأنه عزيز ذو انتقام لكن لما كان هذا التعليل لا يخلو عن حاجة إلى ضميمة

words: شَىْءٌۭ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing in heaven or earth is hidden from God, whether apparent to the senses or absent from them.
rows.anchor: فبين أنه عزيز لا يخفى عليه شيء ظاهر على الحواس ولا غائب عنها

words: شَىْءٌۭ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, 'what is in the earth and heaven' may mean outward deeds done by bodily members and inward acts concealed in hearts.
rows.anchor: ومن الممكن أن يكون المراد مما في الأرض وما في السماء الأعمال الظاهرة القائمة بالجوارح والخفية الكامنة في القلوب
